message:
Amara, Chidi and Dalia, the failed one-tonne field-heat sum is fixed and it explains the mismatch.

Loading one warm tonne at once needs far more than steady holding. The thermal store is 25 kilowatt hours in the pull-down energy (E56), averaging 1040 watts cooling over a day in the pull-down power (E57), or about 12.5 kilowatt hours electric one-off in the steady load simulation (E31). That one-off is about three household days in one day, so it cannot plausibly run in one solar day on this store.

Dalia and Chidi, staging the harvest over three days makes the electrics fit. Loading about 333 kilogrammes per day adds about 8.33 kilowatt hours thermal per day, about 4.17 kilowatt hours electric, plus steady 3.78 kilowatt hours per day in the steady load simulation (E31), giving about 8 kilowatt hours per day matching the array sizing (E16). That suits outside sorting and daily filling.

Amara, the cooler peak must cover staged pull-down plus steady and respiration. Steady cooling is about 315 watts in the steady load simulation (E31), staged extra averages about 350 watts, so a variable-speed Direct Current unit, where Direct Current (DC) means battery-type power, around 1000 watts cooling with Coefficient of Performance near 2, where Coefficient of Performance (COP) means cooling per electricity, meets both. I am not ready, because upsizing the cooling unit (C5) and door openings with Chidi and Dalia must fix peak size.
